clue.text: Left in grip of trendy guy, taking up powdery stuff

indicators.note: the letter for left is held tightly inside the other piece, as if gripped
in a down clue, taking up means the word is read upwards, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a hip, fashionable man

explanation.surface: Someone describes a trendy man picking up some powder, with a left-hand grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' turns CAT into TAC, and 'in grip of' puts L inside it after the TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum is a soft mineral ground into a fine powder for skin care.

clue.text: Odd set on mountains, getting cut off

indicators.note: odd here means strangely arranged, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A strange group placed on high peaks finds itself isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges SET into EST; in a down clue 'on' places it above RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, severing the bond, much as being cut off from family.

clue.text: Romances about present-day women

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other here

parts.note: romances in the sense of fanciful falsehoods are lies
AD (anno Domini) labels the current era, so stands for present-day

explanation.surface: Love stories concerning modern females.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AD inside LIES, giving L-AD-IES; 'Romances' means fibs, not love affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies is a polite plural term for adult females.

clue.text: Data run starts to malfunction at length? That's irregular

parts.note: info is short for information, i.e. data
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A data run begins to fail at length, which looks odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of malfunction, at and length: MAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal arrangements do not follow fixed rules or official procedure, so are casual or unconventional.

clue.text: Match venues remain unfinished before upsurge in support

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for remain loses its last letter

parts.note: to stay is to remain

indicators.note: in a down clue, an upsurge means the word rises, so reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: aid means help or support

explanation.surface: Sports grounds stay incomplete before a rise in backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts STAY to STA; 'upsurge in' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is the Latin plural of stadium, the arenas where sporting fixtures are played.

clue.text: Avignon birds head for home after Navy chief pinching one's bottom in East Anglia area

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the East Anglian area

parts.note: the Fens are low-lying marshland in East Anglia, eastern England

indicators.note: after places the letter from home behind what comes before
pinching means holding a piece squeezed inside another

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: bottom means the last letter of the word one's
head for means take the first letter of home

explanation.surface: Birds from Avignon fly home behind a naval commander who grabs someone's bottom in the Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' puts E (bottom of one's) inside RN, 'head for' takes H from home, placed 'after' CH; all go 'in' FENS between F and ENS. The Fens are a flat fenland region of East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is in France, so its hens are French: the three gifts on the third day of the Twelve Days of Christmas.

clue.text: Death-haunted singers, pale, engaged in heartless songs

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside the other piece
heartless removes the middle letters of songs, keeping the outer pair

parts.note: wan means pale or pallid

explanation.surface: Gloomy singers go pale while performing songs that lack feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves SS from songs, and WAN is 'engaged in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says these birds sing only once, just before dying: hence a swan song.

clue.text: Idiotic boss, Conservative -the usual tale of woe

indicators.note: idiotic means crazy, so the word boss is rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A foolish Conservative boss tells the same old miserable story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idiotic' rearranges BOSS to SOBS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a pitiful account told to win sympathy.

clue.text: Rule broken after relative catching one undressed?

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the relative
catching means holding a letter inside the other word

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
a means one

indicators.note: broken means the letters of rule are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative breaks a rule by catching someone with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts A inside AUNT (AUNAT); 'broken' turns RULE into UREL, placed 'after'. The question mark flags a playful definition: the phrase usually means plainly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in a natural state, often used jokingly for naked.

clue.text: Daughter avoids lazily following line shown by another girl?

indicators.note: following places the trimmed word after the letter for line
avoids means the letter for daughter is left out

parts.note: idly means lazily

explanation.surface: A daughter shirks her lazy ways after another girl shows her the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' drops D from IDLY, giving ILY, placed 'following' L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily is a female first name, so another girl beside the daughter.

clue.text: Upset sailor getting clothing as accompaniment to rum?

indicators.note: upset in an across clue turns the word over, reading it backwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
a cardi is short for cardigan, an item of clothing

explanation.surface: An upset sailor puts on some clothing to go with his rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns AB into BA, then CARDI follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a well-known brand of white spirit distilled from sugar cane.

clue.text: Mouth's suppressing row for second, say

indicators.note: suppressing means keeping the noise held down inside the other word

parts.note: oral means belonging to the mouth
din means a row, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A mouth holds back a quarrel for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' puts DIN inside ORAL. 'second' looks like a unit of time but is an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Second is a number showing position in a sequence, like first or third.

clue.text: Many stayed after crash around track, getting comfort

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps the other
after a crash things are jumbled, so the letters of many stayed are rearranged

parts.note: a path is a track

explanation.surface: Many people stayed on after a crash on the track, receiving consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after crash' rearranges MANY STAYED into TEAANDSYMY, which goes 'around' PATH. In Britain a cup of tea is the classic remedy offered with sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means kindly consolation offered to someone upset, literally a cuppa and a kind word.

clue.text: Bring up missing opening in request seemingly

indicators.note: in means the trimmed word sits inside the word for request

parts.note: to apply is to make a request

indicators.note: missing opening means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to parent a child is to bring it up

explanation.surface: Raising something without a start in a request, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing opening' cuts PARENT to ARENT, which goes 'in' APPLY between APP and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean as far as one can tell, to all appearances.

clue.text: Innocuous story, just a little, relies on ignoring surroundings

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount

indicators.note: ignoring surroundings means dropping the first and last letters of relies

explanation.surface: A harmless story, only slightly exaggerated, depends on ignoring its context.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring surroundings' strips relies to ELIE, placed below WHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmless untruth told to spare feelings is a fib meant kindly.

clue.text: English journalists chasing Queen should be put down

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the English journalists come after the queen

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: English reporters hounding the Queen ought to be suppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' sets E and PRESS behind R.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress a revolt is to crush or quell it.

clue.text: Reproaches about American sanctions

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: stains are marks of disgrace, reproaches

explanation.surface: Criticism about American sanctions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts US inside STAINS after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain an objection is to uphold or approve it, as a judge does.

clue.text: Redesigned the cowl (unsophisticated stuff)

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters of the cowl are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A monk's hood has been remodelled from basic materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic, simple technology is unsophisticated, as opposed to advanced kit.

clue.text: Deep shaft, mostly dark? Nearly

parts.note: a well is a deep shaft sunk into the ground

indicators.note: mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: night means darkness, the dark

explanation.surface: A deep shaft that is mostly in darkness, or almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NIGHT to NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is an old-fashioned way of saying almost.

clue.text: Persons of note getting drunk

definitions.meaning: two great composers, men of musical notes
in Cockney rhyming slang the phrase rhymes with pissed, meaning intoxicated

explanation.surface: Distinguished people getting sozzled.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it, a London (Cockney) habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Two nineteenth-century composers whose names in Cockney slang stand for sloshed.

clue.text: Dash round a river in African capital

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: to hare is to dash, run fast

explanation.surface: Run around a river in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts AR inside HARE after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Oddball seizing diamonds is someone barely observed

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing other pieces inside

parts.note: a nut is an oddball, a crank
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A weirdo grabs some diamonds and is spotted with hardly any clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' puts D and IS inside NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed, so is seen barely dressed.

clue.text: Very satisfied with sticks picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the word is lifted to read upwards, backwards

parts.note: gums means sticks, as glue does

explanation.surface: Someone pleased with some sticks they have collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns GUMS into SMUG; 'sticks' is the verb, glues.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means self-satisfied, too pleased with oneself.

clue.text: Island, almost untouched, with whales

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: in mint condition means pristine, untouched
orca, killer whale, can also serve as a plural

explanation.surface: An island, nearly unspoilt, with whales offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts MINT to MIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca is one of the Balearic islands of Spain in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Performed with girl in Irish location

parts.note: done means performed, carried out
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A show done with a girl somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.

clue.text: English engaged in leg breaking with great

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'English engaged in leg breaking with great (4)', gives GLE+E from wordplay but no word defines GLEE: the definition (likely 'great joy' or similar) appears cut short in the OCR and no scan or search supplies it.
annotationWithheld.clue: English engaged in leg breaking with great

clue.text: Elderly king to croon head off in G&S, displaying jewellery

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside G and S

parts.note: the letters G and S as written, also Gilbert and Sullivan
old means elderly
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly

explanation.surface: An old king sings in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, showing off his jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' cuts SING to ING; OLD, R and ING go 'in' G...S. G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic-opera pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold rings are items of jewellery, the five gifts of the fifth day of Christmas.

clue.text: Recalled some people see Germans as stupid folk

indicators.note: Recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people regard Germans as foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is slang for a silly person, so the plural means a flock of fools.
